description: Rhythm Explorer: a trigger sequencer that makes repeating patterns from a seeded random number generator, with eight clock divisions each given its own density

params.text: Sets the chance that a beat of that division fires, 0% never and 100% always, the values between being an average across patterns. It blinks bright yellow each time the division fires
Draws a fresh seed, and so a fresh pattern, which takes effect at the start of the next phrase; the button stays brightly lit until it does. Trigger RESET at the same time to hear it at once
Sets how many bars make up a phrase, 1 to 16; the lights above show the setting and how far through the phrase the sequencer is. At the end the pattern starts again from bar one
Sets which note value that column counts in, cycling through fifteen values from a 1/2 note down to a dotted 1/32; right-click to pick one from a list
Arms a reset, so the phrase restarts from the beginning; the button glows brightly while it is armed. By default the reset happens on the next clock pulse
Silences the GATE output of that division. A muted division never blocks a division to its right that is set to LIN, and there is no CV for it: use a density of -10V instead
With the RUN input unpatched, each press starts or stops the sequencer and the button is brightly lit while it runs. With that input patched, holding the button inverts the run state
Sets how many 1/4 notes make up a bar, 1 to 16; the lights above it show the setting and how far through the bar the sequencer is
Sets what can stop that division firing: ALL nothing, LIN a division to its left firing at that moment, OFF one merely coinciding, dashes the global setting, two bracketed values a fresh group
Sets the mode used for the OR, XOR ODD and XOR 1 outputs, and the mode of any division whose own button is set to the dashes. ALL, LIN and OFF are the only values here
Silences every division gate output and the OR, XOR ODD and XOR 1 outputs, and each press flips it
Sets what the density sliders cover: unipolar 0% to 100%, or bipolar -100% to 100% for pushing a CV-driven density up and down by hand
Locks the division values, the division and global modes and the density polarity where they stand, so a performance on the sliders cannot knock them
Returns every division density slider to 0%
Lit, the random number generator is never reseeded, so the output keeps changing and no pattern repeats

inputs.text: Takes a 24, 48 or 96 PPQN clock, which is what the whole module is timed from; it expects 24 PPQN until the menu says otherwise, and nothing runs properly without it
A unipolar voltage clamped to 0-10V, sampled at each dice action and used as the seed instead of the internal generator; 10V gives the internal seed back, and 0V stops the pattern repeating
Replaces the internal random numbers with any 0-10V signal, each division sampling it at its own beat. A monophonic cable feeds every division alike; 8 polyphonic channels give each its own
A trigger that arms a reset of the phrase, taken at the next clock pulse or at whatever division Reset timing on the menu is set to
Bipolar CV shifting the density of that division by 10% per volt, added after the slider and the global density have been summed and clamped, so -10V is certain to silence it
Sets the mode of that division from voltage, overriding its button and moving the button to match: 0V ALL, 1V LIN, 2V OFF, 3V the global setting, 4V and 5V the bracketed values
Bipolar CV shifting every division's density by 10% per volt; monophonic moves them together, polyphonic feeds each division its own channel. It is summed and clamped before a division's own CV
Sets the mode from voltage, overriding the global mode button: monophonic feeds every division, polyphonic feeds each its own channel from the left. Voltages are as for a division, capped at 2V
A trigger that draws a fresh seed, taking effect at the start of the next phrase
A high gate runs the sequencer and a low gate stops it. Starting resets the phrase to its beginning
Bipolar CV added to the knob above, linear with 0V standing for 1 and 10V for 16, the sum clamped to that range

outputs.text: A gate for every beat that division fires, also carried on its own channel of the polyphonic gate output
A clock at that division's note value, also carried on its own channel of the polyphonic clock output
Carries whatever seed is in force, whether it came from the SEED input or from the internal generator
Eight channels, one carrying each division's gates
Ten channels: the eight division clocks, then the phrase start pulse on channel 9 and the bar start pulse on channel 10
A gate one clock pulse long at the start of every bar, also sent to channel 10 of the polyphonic clock output
Every division's gates combined into one stream, two divisions striking together giving one beat, filtered by the global mode. Monophonic unless a division opens a new group, which adds a channel
Carries a beat only where an odd number of divisions strike together, an even number cancelling out. Monophonic unless a division opens a new group, which adds a channel
Carries a beat only where exactly one division strikes, simultaneous beats being blocked. Monophonic unless a division opens a new group, which adds a channel
A gate one clock pulse long at the start of every phrase, also sent to channel 9 of the polyphonic clock output
A 1ms trigger at every reset, including the one that happens each time the sequencer starts
10V while the sequencer is running and 0V while it is stopped

notes: nothing is produced until a 24, 48 or 96 PPQN clock is patched into CLOCK and the sequencer is started, either by the RUN button or by a high gate at the RUN input
menu: Clock input PPQN — 24, 48 or 96, and it has to match the clock you patch; the module expects 24 until this says otherwise
Clock output width — Input clock pulse, which copies the incoming pulse, or 50% of the division
Gate output width — Input clock pulse, which copies the incoming pulse, or 50% or 100% of the division
Reset timing — when an armed reset is taken: Input clock pulse, Bar, or a note value from 1/2 down to 1/32, including triplet and dotted values
Fixed 1/4 bar division — counts the bar in 1/4 notes whatever the clock PPQN is; left off, the bar counts 1/4, 1/8 or 1/16 notes as the PPQN is 24, 48 or 96
Add right Rhythm Explorer CV expander — places a Rhythm Explorer CV Expander immediately to the right and sets its side switch to match
Add left Rhythm Explorer CV expander — places a Rhythm Explorer CV Expander immediately to the left and sets its side switch to match
Preset — a Vermona randomRHYTHM factory preset sets the divisions and modes up after that hardware
